There was an apparent clustering of reports of su- bacute thrombosis associated with the use of the sirolimus-elut- ing stent soon after its marketing approval in 2003.1 However, subsequent studies2 and additional data from 2063 patients3 sug- gest that use of the sirolimus-eluting stent is not associated with an excess risk of subacute thrombosis compared with bare-metal stents. 1. Muni NI, Gross TP. Problems with drug-eluting coronary stents—the FDA perspective. N Engl J Med 2004; 351: 1593–5. 2. Jeremias A, et al.
